questions.prompt: For a saturated MOSFET, which expression gives \(C_{gs}\)?
options: \(WLC_{ox}\)
\(\tfrac12WLC_{ox} + C_{ov}\)
\(C_{ov}\) only
\(\tfrac23WLC_{ox} + C_{ov}\)
questions.explanation: In saturation the inversion charge is wedge-shaped, so the gate sees two thirds of the full oxide capacitance, plus overlap along the source edge (reader Eq. 10.1). Half is the triode split; overlap alone is \(C_{gd}\).

questions.prompt: A saturated NMOS has \(W = 10\ \mu\mathrm{m}\), \(L = 0.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}\), \(C_{ox} = 5\ \mathrm{fF/\mu m^2}\) and overlap length \(L_{ov} = 0.05\ \mu\mathrm{m}\). Find \(C_{gs}\) in fF.
questions.explanation: \(\tfrac23(10)(0.5)(5) = 16.7\ \mathrm{fF}\) from the channel plus \(C_{ov} = L_{ov}WC_{ox} = 2.5\ \mathrm{fF}\) (Eq. 10.2): 19.2 fF. Using the full \(WLC_{ox}\) gives 27.5 fF.

questions.prompt: Why is \(C_{gd}\) of a saturated MOSFET only an overlap (plus fringe) term?
options: The channel is pinched off at the drain, so drain voltage no longer changes the channel charge
Because the drain is reverse biased to the body
Because \(C_{gd}\) is always zero
Because the oxide is thicker near the drain
questions.explanation: Past pinch-off the channel charge depends on \(V_{GS}\), not \(V_{DS}\), so the only gate-drain coupling is the gate overlapping the drain diffusion (Eq. 10.3).

questions.explanation: \(C_{gd} = L_{ov}WC_{ox} = 0.04 \times 20 \times 8 = 6.4\ \mathrm{fF}\). No channel term appears in saturation.

questions.prompt: A drain diffusion is \(L_j = 1\ \mu\mathrm{m}\) long and \(W = 10\ \mu\mathrm{m}\) wide, with \(C_{j0} = 1\ \mathrm{fF/\mu m^2}\), \(C_{jsw0} = 0.2\ \mathrm{fF/\mu m}\), built-in potential 0.8 V and grading 1/2. Find \(C_{db}\) in fF at \(V_{DB} = 1.5\ \mathrm{V}\). (The perimeter excludes the edge facing the channel.)
questions.explanation: Area \(L_jW = 10\ \mu\mathrm{m^2}\), perimeter \(2L_j + W = 12\ \mu\mathrm{m}\), so the zero-bias value is \(10 + 2.4 = 12.4\ \mathrm{fF}\). Divide by \(\sqrt{1 + 1.5/0.8} = 1.696\): 7.31 fF (reader Eq. 10.5). Counting all four edges (perimeter 22 µm) overestimates it.

options: \(C_{sb}\), because both of its ends are the same node
questions.explanation: With source and body tied, \(C_{sb}\) is shorted. It returns in the four-terminal model when the source moves relative to the body.

questions.prompt: A MOSFET moves from saturation into deep triode. How is the channel's oxide capacitance shared?
options: Two thirds to the source, none to the drain
All of it to the drain
Roughly half of \(WLC_{ox}\) to the source and half to the drain
All of it to the body
questions.explanation: In triode the channel is continuous from source to drain, so both ends control it about equally. In cut-off there is no channel and the gate couples to the body instead.

questions.prompt: Raising \(V_{DB}\) from 0.5 V to 2 V does what to \(C_{db}\)?
options: Raises it, because more charge is stored
Leaves it unchanged, since it is a fixed parasitic
Turns it into a forward-bias diffusion capacitance
Lowers it, because the drain-body depletion region widens
questions.explanation: \(C_{db}\) is a reverse-biased junction capacitance: \(C \propto 1/\sqrt{1 + V_{DB}/\varphi_{bi}}\). More reverse bias, wider depletion, less capacitance.

questions.explanation: Only the channel part scales with \(L\): \(\tfrac23(4)(0.5)(10) = 13.3\ \mathrm{fF}\) plus an unchanged overlap \(1.2\ \mathrm{fF}\), total 14.5 fF. Doubling the whole old value (7.87 fF) also doubles the overlap, giving 15.7 fF.

questions.prompt: Preview of the Miller effect: in a CS stage with gain \(-A\), why does the small \(C_{gd}\) matter so much at the input?
options: It sees the full gate-to-drain swing \((1 + A)v_{in}\), so it acts like \((1 + A)C_{gd}\) to ground
Because \(C_{gd} > C_{gs}\) in saturation
Because it is in series with \(C_{gs}\)
It does not; \(C_{gd}\) only affects the output
questions.explanation: Current through \(C_{gd}\) is set by the voltage across it, which is amplified by the stage. This is the Miller multiplication.
